newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end easier, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end easier, seen in range.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly lower on Monday but dealers said they expected little movement away from current levels ahead of Japan's quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment due out on Wednesday.
"The tankan will keep the market in a very tight range," said one Singapore futures dealer.
The Nikkei 225 September 1997 contract settled at 20,410 points, down 50 on the day and against the day's high of 20,580.

Dealers said the contract was trading within a 300-point range from 20,350 to 20,650 and looked unlikely to break into new ground unless there was an unexpected jolt on interest rates from the United States or Britain.
Trading through the day was subdued with dealers saying sentiment had benefited from an uneventful Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Denver, Colorado.

"The G7 gave us no surprises, nothing special," said one local futures dealer. He said there had been worries that the United States might put pressure on Japan at the summit over the Japanese trade surplus.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract stood at 382.3 points by mid-afternoon on volume of 827 lots.
